subject: design-technology
title: Foundations: Input, Process, Output
welcome_lead: Crack open an electronic gadget and meet the three-block model that drives every smart product.
meta_desc: Learn input-process-output systems and key electronic components for GCSE D&T.
final_note: You can label any electronic system using the input-process-output model.

concepts.def: Signal entering a system, often from a sensor.
Decision or calculation made inside the system.
Action a system produces, like light or sound.
Light-emitting diode used as an output.
Stores small amounts of electrical charge.

walkthroughs.body_html: Almost every electronic product can be drawn as three blocks: input → process → output. A security light has a PIR input, a control circuit as process and a lamp as output. This model helps designers plan and debug systems.
Resistors limit current and are measured in ohms. Capacitors store charge and smooth signals. LEDs light up when current flows the right way and usually need a series resistor to avoid burning out.

walkthroughs.h2: An LED with a 9 V battery
walkthroughs.body_html: An LED needs 2 V and 20 mA. With a 9 V battery the resistor must drop 7 V at 0.02 A. Using V = IR, the resistor value is 350 ohms, so a standard 360 ohm resistor is chosen.
